title: How a hand is played
summary: Hole cards, the board, the streets and what players can do.

intro.text:
In Texas Hold'em every player gets **two hole cards** that only they can see. During the hand **five community cards** are dealt face up in the middle: the board.

From their two cards and the five on the board, each player makes the **best five-card hand**. The pot goes to the strongest hand, or to the last player left when everyone else has folded.

seats.caption: The button (BTN) is the nominal dealer. To its left sit the small blind (SB) and the big blind (BB). After every hand the button moves one seat clockwise.

blinds.text:
**Blinds** are forced bets posted before the cards are dealt. The small blind is usually half the big blind. Without them nobody would have a reason to play: the pot would be empty.

In this app the blinds are 50/100, and stacks are counted in big blinds: a 10,000-chip stack is 100 BB.

streets.text:
A hand goes through **streets**, each with a betting round:
- **Preflop**: everyone has two cards. The player left of the big blind (UTG) acts first, the big blind last.
- **Flop**: three board cards are dealt.
- **Turn**: the fourth card.
- **River**: the fifth card.

After the flop the first remaining player left of the button acts first, and the button acts last.

labels: River: you have an ace-high straight

actions.text:
When it's your turn you can:
- **Fold**: give up your cards and leave the hand.
- **Check**: pass, if nobody has bet on this street yet.
- **Call**: match the bet.
- **Bet**: be the first to put chips in on a street.
- **Raise**: increase someone else's bet.
- **All-in**: put in all your chips.

In No-Limit Hold'em you can bet any amount up to your stack. The smallest bet is the big blind, and a raise must be at least as big as the previous raise: after a bet of 300 the minimum raise is to 600.

q-first.q: Who acts first preflop at a 6-max table?
q-first.explain: Preflop, the player to the left of the big blind acts first: UTG, "under the gun". The blinds have already put chips in and act last.

showdown.text:
If more than one player is left after the river, there is a **showdown**: cards are shown and the best five-card hand wins the pot. Equal hands split the pot.

But most hands never reach a showdown. Usually the pot goes to whoever bet while everyone else folded. That's why poker is about how you bet, not only about your cards.

t1.q: How many cards are on the board by the river?
t1.explain: The flop is three cards, the turn the fourth, the river the fifth.

options: When nobody has bet on this street yet
t2.explain: A check means "pass". You can only do it when nobody has bet yet. Facing a bet, you can fold, call or raise.

t3.q: Blinds are 50/100 and a player bets 300. What is the smallest raise?
t3.explain: A raise must go up by at least the size of the last increase. The 300 bet went up by 300, so the minimum raise is another 300: to 600.
